newsitem.title: FRANCE: France resumes contacts with Bosnia after deal.
newsitem.headline: France resumes contacts with Bosnia after deal.

text.p: France resumed contacts with the Bosnian embassy in Paris on Friday after U.S. envoy Richard Holbrooke ended a row between Bosnia's squabbling leaders over ambassadorial posts.
"Under these circumstances, France has decided to end the freeze on relations with the Bosnian embassy in Paris," a spokesman for the Foreign Ministry said.
He said the agreement reached by Holbrooke was "a major step towards implementing the peace accord and showed that the determination of the international community had paid off".

France, along with the United States and other western European countries had suspended contacts with Bosnian envoys this week after Moslem, Croat and Serb political leaders failed to agree on the allocation of major posts, especially Washington, by an August 1 deadline.
The Paris spokesman said contacts with Bosnian envoys would be suspended again if Bosnian leaders failed to agree within two weeks on the names of the envoys.
"Whetever their ethnic origin, these ambassadors must from thereon represent a united and sovereign country, as well as all its communities," he said.
Under the deal, the Bosnian ambassador to the United Nations will be a Moslem, a Serb will be ambassador to Washington and a Croat will be ambassador to Japan, Holbrooke and other mediators said.
Bosnia's current ambassadors were appointed by the wartime Moslem-led Bosnian government which fought separatist Serbs and, for 10 months, Croat forces, their nominal allies.
